title: Appendix: Gregory of Valencia on efficacious grace
source_text: CXLI. Ne tamen quaedam paginae hic vacent, summatim adjiciemus, quasi exempli causa, sententiam Gregorii de Valentia Jesuitae satis nobilis, quam plures viri docti referunt & refutant. Ille igitur existimat gratiam efficacem consistere in aliquo dono, quod homo jam praeventus a gratia vocante & excitante, possit cum auxilio Dei consequi, per pium usum sui liberi arbitrii: quodque in uno genere causae, scilicet efficientis, sit natura prius quam ipsa libera conversio; & in alio posterius, scilicet in genere causae materialis atque dispositivae.
pass_a_gloss: CXLI. Yet lest some pages be empty here, we will add in summary, as it were by way of example, the opinion of Gregory of Valencia a Jesuit of sufficient note, which several learned men report & refute. He then thinks that efficacious grace consists in some gift, which a man already prevented by calling & rousing grace, can obtain with the help of God, through the pious use of his free choice: and which in one genus of cause, namely efficient, is prior by nature to the free conversion itself; & in another posterior, namely in the genus of material and dispositive cause.
pass_b_english: Thesis CXLI. So that some pages are not left blank here, we will add in brief, as an example, the opinion of Gregory of Valencia, a Jesuit of some note, which a number of learned men report and refute. He holds that efficacious grace consists in a gift that a person already forestalled by calling and stirring grace can obtain, with God's help, through devout use of his free choice. In one order of cause, the efficient, this gift is by nature prior to the free conversion itself; in another, the material and dispositive, it is posterior.
